## Overview

This PR adds support for the `layer` prop in `FasterAntdStyleProvider` to enable CSS layer wrapping, allowing better compatibility with third-party style libraries like Tailwind CSS, Styled-components, and Emotion.

## Background

When using multiple CSS libraries together, style conflicts can occur due to CSS specificity and ordering issues. Ant Design's `StyleProvider` supports a `layer` prop that wraps styles in a CSS `@layer`, which helps manage style priority and prevents conflicts. However, `FasterAntdStyleProvider` did not previously support this feature.

See the [Ant Design CSS Compatibility documentation](https://ant.design/docs/react/compatible-style) for more context.

## Changes

### API Enhancement

Added an optional `layer` prop to `FasterAntdStyleProvider`:

```tsx
import { FasterAntdStyleProvider } from 'antd-style';

// Without layer (default behavior - unchanged)
<FasterAntdStyleProvider>
  <App />
</FasterAntdStyleProvider>

// With layer support (new feature)
<FasterAntdStyleProvider layer>
  <App />
</FasterAntdStyleProvider>
```

### Implementation Details

- **Minimal changes**: Only 2 source files modified (`FasterAntdStyleProvider.tsx` and `index.ts`)
- **Backward compatible**: Default behavior remains unchanged when `layer` prop is not provided
- **Type-safe**: Exported `FasterAntdStyleProviderProps` interface for TypeScript support
- **Conditional wrapping**: When `layer={true}`, wraps children with `@ant-design/cssinjs`'s `StyleProvider` to enable CSS layer support

### Documentation & Examples

- Comprehensive usage documentation with examples
- Demo files showing both default and layer-enabled usage
- Test cases covering all prop scenarios

## Testing

- ✅ All linting checks pass
- ✅ TypeScript type checking passes
- ✅ Test suite created with coverage for:
  - Default behavior without layer prop
  - Layer prop enabled
  - Boolean prop value handling

## Migration

No breaking changes. Existing code continues to work without modifications. The `layer` prop is optional and defaults to `false`.

author: lox
body:
## Summary

Introduces automatic namespacing of worktrees by repository name to prevent collisions when multiple projects share a parent directory.

## Problem

When multiple projects share a parent directory (e.g., `/projects/myproject` and `/projects/another-project`), their worktrees would collide in `../worktrees`. This forced users to manually create project-specific directories like `../myproject-worktrees` as a workaround.

## Solution

Worktrees are now automatically namespaced by repository directory name:

**Before:**
```
../worktrees/
├── feature/auth      # Could be from any project! 
└── fix/bug-123       # Collision risk
```

**After:**
```
../worktrees/
├── myproject/
│   ├── feature/auth
│   └── fix/bug-123
└── another-project/
    └── feature/new-feature
```

## Key Features

### 1. Auto-Detection for Backwards Compatibility
- **New projects**: Automatically use namespaced layout
- **Existing projects**: Auto-detected based on existing worktrees
- **Legacy projects**: Continue working without changes

### 2. Migration Command
```bash
# Preview migration
wtp migrate-worktrees --dry-run

# Perform migration
wtp migrate-worktrees

# Consolidate from ../myproject-worktrees to ../worktrees
wtp migrate-worktrees --new-base-dir=../worktrees
```

### 3. Configuration
```yaml
defaults:
  namespace_by_repo: true   # Use namespaced layout (default for new projects)
  namespace_by_repo: false  # Use legacy layout (opt-out)
  # Omit for auto-detection based on existing worktrees
```

### 4. Helpful Warnings
When legacy layout is detected, users see:
```
⚠️  Legacy worktree layout detected. Consider migrating to namespaced layout:
   wtp migrate-worktrees --dry-run  # Preview changes
   wtp migrate-worktrees            # Migrate worktrees

   Or to keep current layout, add to .wtp.yml:
   defaults:
     namespace_by_repo: false
```

## Changes

- **Auto-namespace worktrees** by repository directory name
- **Auto-detect** existing layouts for backwards compatibility
- **Add `migrate-worktrees` command** with `--dry-run` and `--new-base-dir` flags
- **Show migration warnings** when legacy layout is auto-detected
- **Config option**: `namespace_by_repo` (true/false/nil for auto-detect)
- **Comprehensive documentation** in README and architecture docs
- **Tests** for migration command and config logic

## Benefits

✅ Multiple projects can safely share `../worktrees`  
✅ No manual workaround with project-specific directories  
✅ Fully backwards compatible with existing setups  
✅ Gradual migration path with helpful warnings  
✅ Optional consolidation from custom base_dir to shared directory

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests pass for config auto-detection
- [x] Unit tests pass for migrate command structure
- [x] Manual testing of migration with --dry-run and --new-base-dir
- [x] Documentation updated

## Files Changed

- `cmd/wtp/migrate.go`: Migration command implementation
- `cmd/wtp/migrate_test.go`: Migration tests
- `internal/config/config.go`: Auto-detection logic and namespacing support
- `internal/config/config_test.go`: Updated tests for namespacing
- `cmd/wtp/list.go`: Added migration warnings
- `cmd/wtp/cd.go`: Added migration warnings
- `cmd/wtp/main.go`: Registered migrate command
- `README.md`: Documentation for namespacing and migration
- `docs/architecture.md`: Architecture documentation

body:
## Summary
- Implements PID tracking for watch processes spawned with --watch
- Adds --list-watch to show tracked watch processes
- Adds --kill-watch to stop all tracked watch processes
- Warns about running processes during --restore

## Problem
When using `bin/swap-deps --watch`, the tool spawns npm watch processes in the background using `Process.spawn`. However, these PIDs were not tracked, which could lead to:
- Orphaned processes accumulating over multiple invocations
- No easy way to stop watch processes
- Resource waste from forgotten background processes

This addresses the highest priority item from issue #37.

## Solution
Implemented comprehensive watch process management:

### PID Tracking
Watch process PIDs are now saved to `~/.cache/swap-deps/watch_pids.json`:
```json
{
  "shakapacker": 12345,
  "react_on_rails": 12346
}
```

### --list-watch
Shows status of all tracked watch processes:
```bash
bin/swap-deps --list-watch
```

Output:
```
🔍 Tracked watch processes:
   shakapacker (PID: 12345) - ✓ Running
   react_on_rails (PID: 12346) - ✗ Not running

   1/2 process(es) are currently running
```

### --kill-watch
Stops all tracked watch processes:
```bash
bin/swap-deps --kill-watch
```

Output:
```
🛑 Stopping watch processes...
```

author: katspaugh
body:
## Summary
This PR improves CI reliability and speed by properly separating unit tests from integration tests into parallel jobs.

## Problem
Unit tests were incorrectly including tests that require real infrastructure (Postgres, Redis, RabbitMQ):
- 13 migration tests in `migrations/deprecated/__tests__/` used `TestDbFactory`
- 7 datasource tests used real database connections
- This made "unit tests" slow and dependent on external services

## Solution
- ✅ Renamed 20 misclassified test files from `.spec.ts` to `.integration.spec.ts`
- ✅ Removed `./migrations` from `jest-unit.json` roots
- ✅ Created separate Jest configs for unit and integration tests
- ✅ Split CI workflow into two parallel jobs
- ✅ Added comprehensive `TESTING.md` documentation

## Test Distribution
| Test Type | Count | Percentage | Infrastructure Required | Execution Time |
|-----------|-------|------------|------------------------|----------------|
| Unit Tests | ~309 | 92% | ❌ None (all mocked) | ~2 minutes |
| Integration Tests | ~27 | 8% | ✅ Postgres, Redis, RabbitMQ | ~5 minutes |
| **Total** | **~336** | **100%** | - | **~5 minutes (parallel)** |

## Benefits
- ⚡ **Faster local development** - Unit tests run without Docker
- 🎯 **Better failure isolation** - Immediately identify if failure is code or infrastructure related
- 💰 **Clearer test organization** - Tests properly classified by their dependencies
- 🛡️ **Improved reliability** - Infrastructure failures don't affect unit test results
- 🚀 **Parallel execution** - Both test suites run simultaneously in CI
- ✅ **Proper separation of concerns** - Unit tests test logic, integration tests test infrastructure

## Usage
```bash
# Local development (fast, no Docker needed)
yarn test
yarn test:unit

# With external services running (requires Docker)
yarn test:integration

# Run everything
yarn test:all
```

## CI Changes
- **unit-tests job**: Runs ~309 unit tests, no external services required
- **integration-tests job**: Runs ~27 integration tests with Postgres, Redis, RabbitMQ
- **tests job**: Aggregates both for branch protection
- Both jobs run in parallel and report coverage to Coveralls
